candidate.answerReason: The mean and range imply that the largest entry is at most 15. Equality would force the other seven entries to be 7, contradicting the median. The collection 6,6,6,8,8,8,8,14 satisfies every condition and attains 14.

methods.label: Bound the total and examine equality
methods.explanation:
The mean fixes the total, while the range gives a lower bound for every entry in terms of the largest one.

Let \(L\) be the largest integer in the collection. Since the range is \(8\), the smallest entry is \(L-8\). Thus each of the other seven entries is at least \(L-8\). The mean is \(8\), so the total is \(8\cdot8=64\), giving
\[
64\ge L+7(L-8)=8L-56.
\]
Consequently, \(L\le15\).

If \(L=15\), the other seven entries are all at least \(7\), and their sum must be \(64-15=49\). They must therefore all equal \(7\). That collection has median \(7\), contradicting the required median \(8\). Since \(L\) is an integer, it follows that \(L\le14\).

To attain \(14\), use
\[
6,6,6,8,8,8,8,14.
\]
The total is \(64\), so the mean is \(8\). The middle two entries are both \(8\), so the median is \(8\). The number \(8\) occurs four times, more than any other number, making it the unique mode. Finally, the range is \(14-6=8\).

Therefore the largest possible integer is \(14\), choice \(\mathrm{D}\).
